problems.statement: The 98.1% on-time figure is a metric artifact: the bonus (tied to TMS on-time %) created an incentive for dispatchers to revise promised dates, and the KPI definition overwrites the original date, so reported on-time no longer measures delivery against customer expectations.
The CEO's explanation that RouteWise plus the bonus genuinely improved on-time delivery is not supported; RouteWise showed only mileage/fuel benefits and Northgate's jump preceded its go-live.

Revisions are legitimate (customer requests or weather), as the Northgate manager says; the data show Customer Request revisions flat per 100 shipments, weather days fewer, and the growth entirely in Operational - Capacity, entered late with little customer notification.

Real service has deteriorated (customers receive freight later than originally promised), with lateness complaints up 35% and Brightwell on-time vs original appointment down from 87% to 81%, while the headline claims improvement.
The rise in complaints is merely a portal reporting artifact.

An underlying driver shortage (vacancy 6.1% to 9.4%, mountain lanes) is a real operational cause of lateness and contributes to Operational - Capacity revisions, though its magnitude is unquantified and confounded.

Management governance failure: nobody monitors revision behavior, supervisors endorse protecting the number, concerns are rarely raised, and the incentive was introduced without revision controls; the customer-facing campaign would make a misleading claim and compound churn risk (Brightwell tender of 30% of lanes).

causalClaims.from: Dispatcher on-time bonus combined with unrestricted date revisions

causalClaims.to: Customer-experienced lateness, complaints and churn risk

actions.action: Halt the 12 January '98 out of 100, on time' campaign and do not substantiate the claim as currently measured.
actions.rationale: The metric is not measured against original customer promises, so the claim is likely misleading and carries legal and reputational exposure.

actions.action: Do not raise the top bonus tier to 99% / $1,500.
actions.rationale: It would intensify the incentive to revise dates and further detach the number from service.

actions.action: Recompute on-time against the original promised/booked date for all shipments (using the revision log) and report it alongside the revised-date figure.
actions.rationale: This gives the true service baseline and a defensible metric.

actions.action: Suspend or redesign the dispatcher bonus: tie it to original-date on-time and add revision controls (reason-code validation, supervisor approval for late or capacity revisions, mandatory customer notification, audit).
actions.rationale: Removes the incentive and the loophole that produced the distortion.

actions.action: Engage Brightwell and other large accounts directly with accurate data and a recovery plan before the Q1 tender review.
actions.rationale: The largest customer already sees lateness and is tendering 30% of lanes.

actions.action: Address driver shortage on mountain lanes through recruitment and capacity planning.
actions.rationale: Likely a real cause of genuine lateness, but its size needs confirmation from original-date analysis.

actions.action: Open an inquiry into supervisor guidance at morning calls and create a safe channel for dispatcher concerns.
actions.rationale: Survey shows pressure to protect the number and little escalation.

actions.action: Attribute the improvement to RouteWise and expand on that basis.
actions.rationale: RouteWise evidence supports only fuel and mileage savings, not on-time gains.

actions.action: Dismiss complaint growth as a portal effect.
actions.rationale: Only lateness complaints rose, damage and billing complaints were flat despite the same portal.

nextEvidence: Original-promised-date on-time % by center, month and terminal from the revision log, Jan 2025 to Sep 2026, versus the reported figure
Northgate on-time and revision trend around RouteWise go-live on 2026-10-19, plus Oct data, and revision rate by dispatcher against bonus tier
Complaint and delivery data from other large accounts compared with their own receiving logs, and lateness complaints split by portal versus phone
output.summary: The 98.1% figure is mostly a measurement artifact. The March 2026 bonus tied pay to on-time % measured against a promised date that dispatchers can overwrite, and revisions rose fivefold, almost all in the capacity reason code, often late and unnotified. Northgate jumped before RouteWise went live there, and RouteWise showed only fuel and mileage gains. Lateness complaints rose 35%, and Brightwell's own logs show on-time falling from 87% to 81% while it is tendering 30% of its lanes. A driver shortage is a plausible genuine cause. Stop the campaign, do not raise the bonus, re-measure against original dates, and fix the incentive and revision controls.
